articles.title: Andy Burnham fails to rule out Brexit reversal being in next Labour manifesto
articles.summary:
PM skirts question and says his focus is on rebuilding bridges before first meeting with Ursula von der Leyen

Andy Burnham has opened the door to fighting the next election on the UK…

blocks.text: Andy Burnham has opened the door to fighting the next election on the UK rejoining the EU, but said his immediate priority was continuing to rebuild bridges with European allies.

The prime minister, who will hold his first meeting with the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, on Tuesday, did not rule out including reversing Brexit in Labour’s next manifesto – but suggested the country should focus on securing closer trading ties first.

Ministers have expressed fears privately that the EU reset has lost significant momentum since Burnham became prime minister, and a summit on the issue is likely to be delayed again unless the bloc agrees to discuss legislation that could lock British business out of parts of EU industry.

Burnham has said he will stick to Keir Starmer’s red lines this side of an election, but he is under pressure from Labour MPs who opposed Brexit to change tack, in part because of the potential boost to growth, even though his own seat of Makerfield voted to leave.

Asked by reporters on his flight to New York on Monday for the UN general assembly whether he could rule out a reversal of Brexit being in the next Labour manifesto, he said: “Our focus at the moment is on a UK/EU summit which we hope will take place later this year.

“My immediate priority is to build on the good work that Keir did in rebuilding bridges. Because those bridges were broken in the early part of this decade. And Keir did a good job in re-establishing that relationship.

“What we have got to do now is go to the next level in terms of reaching practical agreement that will further boost the British economy. And those issues are the substance of the summit alongside EU requests around youth mobility.”

The prime minister admitted he had concerns about the bloc’s “made in Europe” legislation, which is designed to curb China’s increasing presence but could also affect British industry and supply chains.
He said he would share those concerns “in a constructive spirit” with von der Leyen. “The other issues you discuss, they are for another day,” he said of rejoining the bloc.
Burnham said the UK had considerable support among EU member states for its position on the “made in Europe” legislation, which threatens to scupper ongoing negotiations about the reset.
“Europe’s argument is not with us. We both suffer the same effects as other countries, particularly steel,” he said.
after newsletter promotion
“We are making the argument we are not your enemies here ... we are not the problem. ‘Made in Europe’ is dealing with a different problem.”
He also said delicate UK/Ireland supply chains could end up being “collateral damage” of any disagreement with the EU.
“Let’s work towards a trusted partner approach that doesn’t cause a problem where there wasn’t a problem and where we have common cause,” he said.
In his speech to the UN on Tuesday night, Burnham will reflect on the 10 years since Brexit and say the UK needs to be more clear-eyed about the risks to its democratic system.

“I’m reflecting on that last decade,” he told reporters on his plane. “What we’ve experienced is when that turbulence comes, when outside actors seek to manipulate, to distort facts, influence the British democratic process.
“Going into the next decade we need to be clear-eyed about that and become stronger and more on the front foot about challenging that.

“Perhaps Britain can say we have experienced some of the turbulence before others in terms of the politics of recent times. We need to be clearer where outside forces, our enemies, are trying to manipulate that opinion and feeling to serve their interests, not ours.”

articles.title: 'Father of Nunavut' has one more fight left: to live in the territory he helped create
articles.summary: Supporters of John Amagoalik are helping him take the Nunavut government to court as a last resort to force the territory to pay his living expenses so he can spend his final days at home.

image.caption: Amagoalik, who turns 79 in November, is shown in Iqaluit. The Nunavut government declined his request to provide adequate funding for his care and accessible housing, so he's going to court. (Juanita Taylor/CBC)

blocks.text: He helped found Nunavut, now he’s fighting to age there
"I'll never go back," John Amagoalik said of an assisted living facility in Ottawa, where he was sent to live by Nunavut's government in February 2025.
The territory's Department of Health transferred him to Embassy West Senior Living after an infection left no choice but to amputate part of his right leg.
"The worst part was the loneliness," Amagoalik recalled in an interview with CBC News as he sat in a wheelchair at his temporary home in Iqaluit with his wife, Evie, on Sept. 7.
"The strange surroundings. That was the worst part, being so far away from home and not ... being able to be with my many grandchildren."
Amagoalik is turning 79 in November and has multiple chronic age-related issues. He also has a difficult time talking.
He's frail, but he's still a fighter.

After a lifetime of struggle that included being forced to attend residential schools and advocating for Inuit rights and self-determination, Amagoalik is in his last fight: to age in the territory he helped create.
"It's been my life," he said, when asked what Nunavut means to him. "And I feel fortunate in being part of it."
'Father of Nunavut'
John Amagoalik is revered as the "Father of Nunavut" for his work spanning over three decades beginning in the 1970s — earning him the Order of Nunavut and the Order of Canada.

Among his many roles, he advocated for Inuit as an adviser with the Tunngavik Federation of Nunavut before it became Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. He was also on the executive council of the Inuit Circumpolar Council in the 1980s, and served as president of what was then the Inuit Tapirisat of Canada, now Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami.

Amagoalik led the land claims settlement process with Nunavut Tunngavik after ratification in 1993. He also chaired the Nunavut Implementation Commission that designed the public government of Nunavut before the territory was created in 1999.
It's the very government his Victoria-based lawyer and longtime friend, Steve Kelliher, said is now failing him. So he's helping Amagoalik take the Nunavut government to court.

items: Mounties spied on 'Father of Nunavut' in 1970s amid fears of Inuit-Dene alliance

blocks.text: Kelliher, who first worked with Amagoalik in the 1970s formulating Nunavut's future government, said his friend is still as much a force today as he was back then.

But when he and another friend, Mark Stiles of Ottawa — who first met Amagoalik in 1975 while working in the land claims office of the Inuit Tapirisat of Canada — visited Amagoalik at Embassy West in March, they felt he needed their help.
"I said, 'Well, how do you like it here, John?' And he said, 'I hate it,'" Kelliher said.
So he asked Amagoalik if he wanted help to return home. "He said, 'Do anything to get me out of here, to get me back to Iqaluit.'"
So they did.
First, they delivered a letter to the territory’s health minister, signed by Amagoalik and dated March 31, pleading to return home. Amagoalik claims he never agreed to the move being permanent.
When the minister, Janet Pitsiulaaq Brewster, didn't take any action on his request to return home, they formed the John A. Committee and brought in Iqaluit lawyer Anne Crawford.

The committee raised $30,000 for a consultant to develop Amagoalik's plan of care, buy medical equipment and supplies, and pay for eight to 10 hours of daily private home care from personal support workers.

It also secured an accessible unit at a subsidized rate of $2,000 a month that has space for his hospital bed and an elevator. The Amagoaliks' public housing unit has stairs that would be too difficult for him to use.
The committee also arranged air transportation donated by an airline to fly Amagoalik to Iqaluit. On June 12, 16 months after he arrived in Ottawa, he returned home.
An uncertain future
But despite all of the hard work to bring Amagoalik back to Nunavut, his future is still uncertain.
The funds raised by the committee were only meant to be for the short term, and Anne Crawford said the money is running out.

"Which we did tell the government at the time, this will not last forever. And therefore, can you talk to us about how and what we can do going forward to continue to support him and live in his home community?"

The request to the territorial government for $16,000 a month to cover accommodations in the accessible unit and up to 10 hours a day of support worker care was declined. However, the government can provide a maximum of two hours per week of personal support worker care.
The committee says its research shows that Nunavut was spending about $30,000 a month for Amagoalik’s care at Embassy West.

items: Coming home: Elders return to Nunavut for care after years of living in the south

blocks.text: The Health Department told CBC News that it can't comment on his care in order to protect his privacy. Brewster, the health minister, also declined to be interviewed.

But a communications manager provided a written statement saying the government has not refused to provide publicly funded health care to Amagoalik and that it continues to work in "good faith to support him."
"So we have no alternative but to appeal to the courts to compel them to do the right thing," Kelliher said, calling the situation "despicable."
"If we've got no money, we'll go beat the bushes," he said. Amagoalik "deserves better. He's earned it. He is an exception. Who treats their leaders like that? Not the Inuit. I don't believe it."
Lack of care facilities for seniors
On Sept. 16, two notices of application for judicial review were filed in the Nunavut Court of Justice on behalf of Amagoalik.

"One for judicial review of the assistant deputy minister's letter, the decision not to fund John's care and housing," Kelliher said. "And an application for urgent relief to compel them to do so until the matter is fully heard, which could take months."

Amagoalik's care situation is emblematic of a wider problem in Nunavut. The vast territory, which covers a total area of just over two million square kilometres and is home to roughly 40,000 people, has only six seniors' facilities spread across its three regions.

items: Amagoalik among 6 northerners appointed to Order of Canada
John Amagoalik, ‘Father of Nunavut,’ honoured in Iqaluit

blocks.text: The government says it's expanding two more long-term care facilities in Nunavut.
Currently, 73 elders from Nunavut are being cared for at Embassy West Senior Living, the only out-of-territory facility contracted by the government for more complex needs.

"We don't want to continue seeing our elders getting flown to Ottawa,” said Gloria Uluqsi, president of Nunavut Tunngavik. "I think they can do better. I think we as a team can do better for our elders."

articles.title: Firm in VP Sara's SALN won millions in Davao City contracts
articles.summary: A company that Vice President Sara Duterte declared as one of her business interests won nearly P36 million in government contracts during her term, almost a third from the Davao City government, a…

blocks.text: September 22, 2026 | 3:59pm

MANILA, Philippines – A company that Vice President Sara Duterte declared as one of her business interests won nearly P36 million in government contracts during her term, almost a third from the Davao City government, a procurement official testified on Tuesday, September 22.

Rendel Sopeña, division chief of the Electronic Government Procurement Operations Division of the Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS), told the Senate impeachment court that the government's procurement database shows 49 contracts awarded to Gencorp Industries Inc.

The City of Davao awarded 15 of the 49 contracts, worth P34.22 million, while PhilHealth Region 11 awarded 33 contracts worth P1.33 million. The Overseas Workers Welfare Administration Region 11 awarded one contract worth P330,000.
The contracts, worth P35,878,188 in all, were awarded between July 21, 2022 and June 23, 2026, according to the summary cited by Presiding Officer Sen. Chiz Escudero.
Prosecutors confirmed that none of the awards predated Duterte's term as vice president.

Sopeña's testimony today comes as the House prosecution continues its presentation of evidence for Article II, which accuses Duterte of accumulating unexplained wealth. The prosecution said Duterte herself declared in her 2024 and 2025 statements of assets, liabilities, and net worth (SALNs) that she is a Gencorp shareholder.
The 1987 Constitution expressly bars the president and vice president from participating in any business during their tenure.

Gencorp's corporate records, however, do not list Duterte as a stockholder or director, Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Director Gerardo Del Rosario testified yesterday and confirmed again today during the tail-end of his testimony.
Escudero said the senator-judges would and should weigh both pieces of evidence.

But lead prosecutor Rep. Jinky Luistro (Batangas, 2nd District), who conducted the direct examination for Sopeña, argued that Duterte's own declaration is the stronger document, given it was she who prepared her own SALN.
"The admission came from the respondent herself," Luistro said.
Gencorp and 'Jollibee Bolton'

Sopeña said he searched the PhilGEPS database for the merchant name "Gencorp Industries Inc." in response to the court's subpoena. He said he extracted 231 documents totaling 484 pages, then printed, certified, and signed each one.
Among the Davao City contracts Sopeña identified were one worth P5.14 million and another worth P6.28 million. Another document was a request for quotation from the city for catering services.
The OWWA contract was covered by a memorandum of agreement between OWWA's Region 11 office and "Jollibee Bolton."

Sopeña read from the document that Jollibee Bolton is under Gencorp Industries Inc. and is a franchise of Jollibee Foods Corporation. When Luistro asked whether this was the Jollibee known to the public, a question the defense had objected to, the PhilGEPS official said he was "not familiar."
Sopeña stressed that the data in PhilGEPS come from the government agencies themselves, which are responsible for encoding procurement details and uploading documents.
Defense counsel Roberto Batungbacal noted that the contracts were awarded after Duterte was no longer mayor of Davao.
"So it is clear your honor that these contracts were awarded during the time that the vice president was not in the city of Davao anymore," Batongbacal said.
Escudero, however, did not carry this objection given that the documents are relevant to the trial precisely because it did not cover the period in which she was mayor of Davao City.
"If she was still the mayor I would not have allowed it because it would have been irrelevant for our purposes," Escudero said.
Batungbacal also objected to the line of questioning on relevance.

To this, Luistro countered that the evidence relates to the final subsection of Article II, which accuses Duterte of non-divestment of business and financial interests. "And it is along this line that we are showing the participation of the respondent by way of the evidence being presented with respect to Gencorp Industries Incorporated," Luistro said.
Luistro's request for judicial notice
At the end of her direct examination, Luistro asked the court to take judicial notice of, or formally accept without proof, several points.
The first was that an Ombudsman records official had already testified on Duterte's 2024 and 2025 SALNs, in which Luistro said Duterte declared Gencorp shares acquired in 2013.

She also cited Article VII, Section 13 of the Constitution and two provisions of Republic Act 12009. Under those provisions, the head of a procuring entity approves the recommendations of the Bids and Awards Committee, and for local governments that head is the local chief executive.
Luistro said the official who approves such resolutions in Davao City is Mayor Sebastian Duterte.
Batongbacal objected that these were not proper subjects of mandatory judicial notice.
Escudero took judicial notice of the laws Luistro cited, "but not as to the interpretation meaning nor application of those laws according to the view of one party only."
He said any family relationship involving Basye would have to be proven when the mayor takes the witness stand.
The vice president's brother is among the prosecution's upcoming witnesses.
Escudero also noted that while Duterte's SALNs presented in court mention Gencorp, the prosecution's own SEC witness testified that Gencorp's records do not show her as a stockholder or director.
He said the court takes notice of both, and left it to the senator-judges to "evaluate, and weigh the testimony of those witnesses."
What the SEC records show
On Monday and Tuesday, Del Rosario testified that Duterte does not appear as an incorporator, director, or stockholder of Gencorp.
Del Rosario said Gencorp's sales from 2021 to 2024 topped P1 billion, but the company declared no dividends in those years.

Earlier on Tuesday, Escudero had Del Rosario compare Duterte's SALNs with SEC records. Her 2024 SALN declares her a stockholder of Gencorp, with an entry suggesting the firm was formerly two other companies.
SEC records show three separate firms, none of which lists her.
Asked how the two could be reconciled, Del Rosario said Duterte might hold her interest through a trust arrangement, or through control of a corporate shareholder.
Sopeña will return for cross-examination on Monday, September 28, at 10 a.m.
The court will not hear witnesses on Wednesday, September 23.
It will instead hold oral arguments on whether the court should overturn Escudero's ruling that 16 of 24 votes are needed to convict Duterte.
Prosecutor Rep. Leila de Lima (Mamamayang Liberal) will argue for the prosecution, while the defense will name its lawyer on Wednesday.

articles.title: Australia investigating how F-35 fighter jet parts bound for US went missing in Hong Kong
articles.summary: Disappearance of jet components sparks concern some of the program’s technology secrets could have been exposed

blocks.text: Richard Marles says the Department of Defence is examining how F-35 fighter jet parts bound for the US from Australia were unexpectedly diverted to Hong Kong.

The acting prime minister said “very much everything that has occurred at the Australian end” will be reviewed, however, he claimed the technology parts were not “sensitive”, as first reported by Politico over the weekend.

The parts, which were being transported by another unknown third party on behalf of manufacturer, Lockheed Martin, still remain unaccounted for months later following their unplanned diversion to Hong Kong.

The last known location of the fighter jet components – in Hong Kong, a special administrative region of China – has sparked concern that some of the program’s technology secrets could have been exposed.

“We are examining [Australia’s involvement], but the point I would make here is that we are confident about the way in which we’ve engaged with the program, and through the US’s prime contractor, Lockheed,” Marles said on Tuesday.
“My understanding is that there is a sense of comfort, and we’re not talking about sensitive equipment here, or sensitive parts.
“Ultimately, though, this is an issue which is going to be managed by the United States and by Lockheed in terms of what has occurred.”
Politico reported sources said the “sensitive” shipment contained on of the jet’s canopies, which reportedly contains stealth technology.
The Guardian has contacted the Pentagon.

While many details have not yet been revealed, Michael Shoebridge, a director for Strategic Analysis Australia who has worked in intelligence agencies, said there were two reasons why China, or another adversary, would want F-35 parts – to reverse engineer them, or to learn how to better exploit and attack them.
Shoebridge added the shipment’s pitstop in Hong Kong was “such an unexpectedly stupid thing” for the manufacturer or Australia to do.

“This is an act of incredible ineptitude and stupidity, and so it’s more the Chinese taking advantage of an incredible stroke of luck brought to them by the stupidity of the people involved,” he said.

Last week, the US State Department announced that the Trump administration would continue with the sale of 48 F-35s to Saudi Arabia, despite reported concerns from the US intelligence community that China could obtain some of the stealth technology.
Australia was one of the early development partners in the F-35. The program spreads the development, supply, management and sustainment of the fighter jets across different countries.

More than 70 Australian companies have production and sustainment contracts with the F-35 program. In excess of 700 of the fighter jet’s “critical pieces” are manufactured in Victoria alone, according to the state government. Australia also hosts a regional distribution hub for F-35 parts in New South Wales.
Australian companies involved in the program’s supply chain have been awarded contracts valued at over $5.2bn, as of September 2025.
Shoebridge said the missing shipment of parts could mean the whole multibillion-dollar fleet is vulnerable to adversaries.
“They’re all now carrying the risk of whatever vulnerabilities this has brought to the to the aircraft,” he said.
“So it’s not just a US-Australia issue. It’s every operator of the F3-5 program [that] has an interest in understanding what happened and what was potentially exposed.”

articles.title: ‘Chicken lollipops’ shipment contained onions, carrots — BOC
articles.summary: In a statement issued Tuesday, September 22, 2026, the BOC said that the charges stem from six shipments consigned to Berches Consumer Goods Trading.

blocks.text: September 22, 2026 | 3:31pm
Bureau of Customs in Manila.
PhotoPhilia via Wikimedia Commons

MANILA, Philippines — The Bureau of Customs (BOC) has filed six criminal complaints before the Department of Justice against an importer, a licensed customs broker, several Customs officers, and other individuals over the alleged misdeclaration of agricultural shipments containing thousands of sacks of fresh onions and carrots.
In a statement issued Tuesday, September 22, 2026, the BOC said the charges stem from six shipments consigned to Berches Consumer Goods Trading.
According to the BOC, the shipments, which arrived in June 2025, were declared as "chicken lollipops."
However, physical examinations conducted by BOC inspectors uncovered 15,029 sacks of fresh white onions and 2,164 boxes of fresh carrots concealed inside the containers.
The agricultural goods lacked the mandatory Sanitary and Phytosanitary Import Clearance from the Bureau of Plant Industry.

The criminal complaints cite violations of Republic Act No. 10863, also known as the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act (CMTA), specifically Section 1401, or Unlawful Importation or Exportation, in relation to Sections 140, or Misdeclaration, and 117, or Regulated Importation and Exportation.

In addition, the involved BOC officials and personnel face charges under Sections 1431 (c), (e), and (f) of the CMTA. The said provisions penalize willful neglect of duty, aiding or abetting acts that defraud the government of customs revenues, and permitting violations of customs law.
Concurrently, the Customs Intelligence and Investigation Service endorsed administrative charges against the implicated Customs personnel to the Prosecution and Litigation Division.
The division will conduct administrative proceedings pursuant to the Revised Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service, according to the BOC.

articles.title: Germany: Chancellor Merz braces for difficult days ahead
articles.summary: Germany's far-right AfD and the socialist Left Party gained ground in recent state elections, while the centrist parties lost support. The biggest loser is Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

image.caption: Chancellor Friedrich Merz is under pressure following the election defeats in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western PomeraniaImage: Annegret Hilse/REUTERS

blocks.text: Why have the results of the two German state elections held on Sunday, September 20, thrown the spotlight on the federal government led by the Christian Democrats (CDU) and its chancellor Friedrich Merz?

For the first time, the party failed to reach the required 5% of votes to enter parliament in the northeastern coastal state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. It marks the first time in its history that the CDU has failed to enter a state parliament. In the city-state of Berlin, where the CDU was incumbent, the party suffered heavy losses and is likely to end up on the opposition benches.

The chancellor says he is aware of the significance. "This election is a profound turning point. It is a dramatic and unprecedented result for the CDU in Germany that we could not clear the 5% threshold. For an entire bloc to leave the state parliament is a heavy blow, and that will resonate with us for a long time to come," he said.
German state elections reveal increasingly polarized country

At the same time, Merz conceded that federal policy, which had failed to convince the public, had played a role in the defeats. Most voters are also not satisfied with the chancellor himself. However, he also sees another cause: "We are experiencing a dramatic shift of the party-political system in Germany, as are many other countries," Merz said.

The chancellor pointed to the competition at the political margins: "In [Sunday's] elections, more than 40% of the vote went to forces which are destructive, which question our political, parliamentary system. And who attempt to excite people with radical and simple solutions," was his analysis. Merz did not name the parties he was referring to, but he clearly meant the Alternative for Germany (AfD) and the Left Party.

The AfD is classified as "confirmed right-wing extremist" by the Office for the Protection of the Constitution, Germany's domestic intelligence agency, in five of Germany's 16 federal states — but not in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, both regions in which it was able to significantly grow its share of the vote.

In the German capital, the AfD's result grew from 9% to 16% compared to the previous election. In the northeastern coastal state, the party more than doubled its result, to 38%. AfD co-leader Tino Chrupalla said, alluding to his party's color: "The blue wave cannot be stopped."
Criticism of the CDU's 'firewall' policy

The AfD's other co-leader Alice Weidel, concluded that the CDU had been pulverized and that the chancellor's resignation is "overdue." "This clearly shows that we have replaced the CDU as the party of the masses," she said.

"That is also the result of a very unintelligent firewall policy," Weidel added, referring to the CDU's so-called resolution of incompatibility, which rejects coalitions with both her party and the socialist Left.

The AfD's claim to have taken the place of the CDU is unfounded, according to political scientist Wolfgang Muno from the University of Rostock in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. The AfD is no big tent party representing conservative interests, he told DW: "It is a right-wing extremist party which has managed to bring together various groups."

Muno's opinion of the Left Party is vastly different to Merz's: "We have seen that the Left has really moved toward being a pragmatic, democratically oriented party. Therefore, there is no reason for the Christian Democrats to simply accuse them of being extremists, because the Left is not an extremist party," Muno said.
The Left Party faces antisemitism allegations

Muno considers criticism of Israeli policies legitimate. At the same time, he notes that it had been accompanied by antisemitic incidents . He expects the Left to send a clear signal that such things are not acceptable. "But not being open to cooperating with a democratic Left Party is, in my opinion, a bad sign," he said, referring to the CDU.

In Berlin, the socialist Left with lead candidate Elif Eralp succeeded in doubling its previous result to 26% and won an election in the city-state for the first time. A scandalous campaign event appearance by rapper Dahabflex, who sang about wishing death for Israel's soldiers, appears not to have damaged the party. Its district association in Neukölln, which had invited the singer, said it intended to clarify the matter.

Josef Schuster, President of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, is skeptical: "So far there have been no personnel or political consequences." He appealed to the Social Democrats and Greens not to form a coalition with the Berlin election winners.

Federal co-leader of the Left, Ines Schwerdtner, told DW that she would not tolerate antisemitism among the party's ranks. "We are there in Berlin to build bridges — Elif Eralp is doing that. And within the party we will absolutely ensure that something like this does not happen."

Eralp, whose parents fled to Germany after a military coup in Turkey, could become the first mayor from the Left in Berlin. About 200,000 of the German capital's four million residents have Turkish roots.

Against this background, the lead candidate considers her and her party's success as an important sign: "I view this election result also as a victory for solidarity, for diversity, for democracy, against the shift to the right which we are experiencing in many places in this country," she said.
Why Germany's political center is losing ground
Merz vows to push through with welfare reforms

Manuela Schwesig, the Social Democrats' (SPD) lead candidate in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, scored a partial success. With about 36% of the vote, her party came in just behind the AfD, but she has good prospects of being able to remain state premier: "I will propose to my party that we hold talks with both the Greens and the Left — the two democratic parties represented in the state parliament — and fulfil our electoral mandate," she said.

The incumbent, who has held the office since 2017, is critical of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's announcement that he wants to press on with his course of deep cuts to the welfare system. The most controversial is the planned pension reform. "He is misjudging the situation of what the people on the ground think, at least in my state," Schwesig said.

She reminded Merz of the agreement his party made with the SPD at the federal level: "I would like for the coalition to implement exactly what we negotiated together in the coalition agreement, namely that the pension without deductions remains possible after 45 years of contribution."
This agreement is currently hanging in the balance. Like the SPD's Schwesig, some eastern German CDU state premiers have spoken out against the chancellor's plans.

Despite this, the SPD faces a dilemma because at the federal level it is part of the government with the CDU. The party's co-leader, Bärbel Bas , now wants to draw the "correct conclusions" from the results of the state parliament elections.

However, she also said that the party had taken responsibility in the federal government. "We are in this coalition, and we also want to maintain it. Nevertheless, we must also accept the analysis from the campaign trail that the people are not satisfied with the upcoming reforms. That means that we, together with our coalition partner, must seek solutions."
This article was translated from German.

articles.title: Princess Diana's brother makes explosive claims about royals in new memoir
articles.summary: Here are some of the key revelations from Charles Earl Spencer's highly anticipated memoir "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister." It has already provoked Buckingham Palace to react.

image.caption: Princess Diana's fatal car crash happened nearly 30 years ago, in August 1997Image: John Shelley Collection/LFI/Photoshot/picture alliance

blocks.text: In the new book "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister," Charles Spencer, the 9th Earl Spencer, offers his perspective on the life of his late sister, Diana, Princess of Wales.

As British tabloid culture ensures that every feud and controversy linked to the royal family gets amplified into a major public debate, the memoir started making headlines before its publication on September 22.

Among some of the key revelations of the book, he says that he believes that Diana had ADHD, and that "as part of that condition she suffered from Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria," which he describes as "an intense emotional pain in the face of others' rejection or criticism."

Spencer also claims their father developed a "romantic connection" with the future Queen Elizabeth II, until he was warned off her by Lord Mountbatten, who was the maternal uncle and close mentor of the queen's husband, Prince Philip.
But most polemically, Spencer revisits one of the British royal family's most painful chapters: the aftermath of Diana's tragic death in a car crash on August 31, 1997.

blocks.caption: 'Swan Song: Diana, My Sister' has been translated into 12 languages for its global release on September 22Image: Penguin Random House/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: 'We'll forget her soon enough'
Spencer writes that when Queen Elizabeth II first heard of Diana's accident, her initial reaction was: "What is she up to now?" before the gravity of the situation became clear.

Diana's death sparked a global outpouring of grief. In the aftermath of the car crash, the royals faced strong public backlash for their delayed and cold response to the tragedy. The Queen's first public address came five days after Diana's death.

In his book, Spencer suggests that some inside Buckingham Palace were "relieved — indeed pleased" that she had died. He also recounts a phone conversation with King Charles, then-Prince of Wales that happened days after her death. According to Spencer, the prince sounded "giddily elated — like a lottery winner."

Spencer writes that they discussed how he objected to having Prince William, then 15, and Prince Harry, then 12, walk behind their mother's coffin during the funeral procession at the internationally televised funeral.

Spencer felt it would be traumatic to put the boys in the media spotlight just after their mother had died. He writes in the book that he believes the boys were used as a protective shield for Charles, as Buckingham Palace officials feared "members of the public might shout abuse at him," whereas the children's presence "would surely guarantee against insults flying."

blocks.caption: From left to right: Earl Spencer, Prince William, Prince Harry and Prince Charles following the coffin to the funeral of Diana, Princess of Wales in 1997Image: Photoshot/picture alliance

blocks.text: Spencer also recounts Diana's belief that Prince Charles had already become jealous of her popularity decades earlier.

He describes how Prince Charles went into a "stream of anger" during the phone conversation after her death. The princess's brother writes that her former husband unleashed "his pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death. 'Rest assured,' he hissed, 'we'll forget her soon enough!'"

But nearly 30 years after the fatal car crash, Diana remains a global icon. The 36-year-old was a glamorous celebrity, renowned for her advocacy for different causes, including her groundbreaking support for AIDS patients.

Buckingham Palace directly reacted to the first excerpt published in the Daily Mail: "While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle. His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss."

In contrast, the Palace met Prince Harry's accusations in his 2023 memoir "Spare" with total institutional silence, applying the royals' traditional public relations strategy of "Never complain, never explain."
Speaking on behalf of the 'blood family'
The feud between Earl Spencer and Buckingham Palace is not new.

Spencer famously delivered a passionate eulogy for his sister at Westminster Abbey in 1997. In it, he not only criticized the role of the paparazzi in the accident, calling his sister the "most hunted person of the modern age," but also set himself apart from the royals by referring to his blood ties with Diana in a promise to protect her boys "from a similar fate."

"I pledge that we, your blood family, will do all we can to continue the imaginative way in which you were steering these two exceptional young men so that their souls are not simply immersed by duty and tradition but can sing openly as you planned," he said at the time.

blocks.caption: Charles Spencer, 9th Earl Spencer, has sparked a highly publicized feud with the royal family with his new memoirImage: Jordan Pettitt/empics/picture alliance

blocks.text: On the day of the funeral, Spencer writes, Queen Elizabeth II offered through intermediaries to posthumously restore Diana's "Her Royal Highness" (HRH) title. Spencer declined, as he felt the gesture had little meaning after her death.
Even though Buckingham Palace has always insisted Diana gave up the title voluntarily, Spencer writes that she was left "dreadfully hurt" by its removal amid her divorce with Charles.
Intrusive tabloid culture led to her death
In his book, Spencer returns to the themes he addressed in his eulogy, accusing the editors and publishers who bought intrusive photos of Diana of having contributed to killing his sister.
According to him, British tabloid culture turned into system that profited from Diana's suffering and encouraged increasingly extreme invasions of privacy.

After the divorce, large sections of the media began portraying Diana as unstable, manipulative, difficult or attention-seeking. Paparazzi would provoke distress and photograph her reaction; newspapers would then publish stories suggesting she was unstable.

She was unable to escape media scrutiny, making her extremely unhappy: "It is a sad fact that, in her later years, Diana drove herself more than once to Beachy Head, the highest chalk sea cliff in England, while contemplating ending it all," Spencer writes, adding: "Her love for her sons stopped her from going further."
A lucrative release ahead of 30th anniversary of Diana's death

While Spencer has long criticized the destructive nature of the British tabloid system, the promotion of his memoir relies on the exact ecosystem he decries. He has sold serialization rights of the book to the UK's Daily Mail — one of the very tabloid outlets frequently associated with intense royal scrutiny.

blocks.caption: According to her brother, Diana already knew on her wedding day that the man she was marrying did not truly love herImage: AFP

blocks.text: Some critics accuse him of wanting to cash in on the tragedy, with the high-profile book published just ahead of the 30th anniversary of Diana's death.

His supporters however feel that Diana's brother is justified to share his personal perspective on their shared experience, noting that many other authors have profited off her legacy over the decades.

Spencer has stated that his account aims to correct decades of "untruths that have become accepted over time" and inaccurate portrayals of his late sister by outside biographers and commentators over the years.

"At heart, this is a brother's simple tribute to an extraordinary sister," Earl Spencer wrote of his own work on Instagram, adding, "A month ago I read 'Swan Song' out, over three days, for a recording so that it could be available on audiobook. When I finished the recording, I thought: 'That is exactly what I wanted and needed to say — and she would, I reckon, have approved of every word.'"

articles.title: Middle East crisis live: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards warns it will ‘change geography of war’ if US escalates conflict
articles.summary:
The US president said in an interview ahead of the United Nations meeting that he was considering ‘wiping Iran out’

Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps warned it would “change the geography of…

blocks.text: IRGC warns it will 'change the geography of the war' if US escalates the conflict
Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps warned it would “change the geography of the war” if the US escalates the conflict, after Donald Trump issued fresh threats against the Islamic Republic.

In an interview with Fox News on Sunday, Trump said “very big things are going to be happening in the not-so-distant future”, adding that the options he was considering were “wiping Iran out, letting them rot economically or making a deal”.

A spokesperson for the IRGC, Hossein Mohebbi, responded with a warning that if the US were to launch fresh attacks against Iran, Tehran would use “new weapons with capabilities into the battle”. “If a new aggression takes place, we will definitely change the weapons and geography of the war,” Mohebbi was quoted as having said.
“Our targets will no longer necessarily be the same as before,” he said, according to the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting, adding that Iran has targets that have not yet been struck.

blocks.caption: Donald Trump is wrestling with an unpopular war and low approval ratings ahead of November’s US midterm elections. Photograph: Evan Vucci/Reuters

blocks.text: The comments come as the US and Iran remain locked in an impasse over the strait of Hormuz and after attacks on the Saudi capital, Riyadh, by Yemen’s Iranian-backed Houthi rebels.

The Houthis, who operate independently of Iran’s instructions, have seized territory along the country’s Red Sea coastline, including near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital shipping route that links Asia to Europe via the Red Sea and Suez canal.

The Houthis have also attacked oil facilities and other types of infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, in response for Saudi airstrikes on Houthi-controlled areas of Yemen. The attacks have further disrupted energy markets, pushing up global fuel prices, including in the US, where consumers have been hit hard.

Iran hugely benefits from the Houthis fighting Saudi Arabia, as the Saudis are more likely in turn to put pressure on the US to relent over Iran, which has insisted it will not allow the reopening of the strait of Hormuz until all its conditions have been met.
With diplomatic negotiations stalled, traffic in the strait continues to be severely disrupted, with Iran firing on commercial ships and demanding it first approve passage along its authorised route.
In response, the US, which started the war on Iran alongside Israel in February, is maintaining a counter-blockade of Iranian ports while intensifying economic pressure.
The US has also fired on commercial shipping in the region and has killed Iranian civilians in its strikes.

articles.title: Brigitte Bardot’s personal items sell for nearly €1m at auction in Paris
articles.summary:
Dog collars, guitars and self-portraits among 285 objects, with money going to her animal welfare foundation and son

An auction of the French film star turned animal rights activist Brigitte…

blocks.text: An auction of the French film star turned animal rights activist Brigitte Bardot’s personal items has fetched nearly €1m (£858,000, US$1.15m, A$1.61m) in Paris, almost 20 times the estimate, according to the auction house Millon.

A total of 285 objects were auctioned, ranging from straw hats, sunglasses and nightgowns to tableware and furniture from Bardot’s homes in Paris and Saint-Tropez, Agence France-Presse (AFP) reported.

Bardot, who died in December aged 91, retired from acting in the 1970s and became an outspoken campaigner for animal rights. She also became increasingly active politically on the far right, alienating some fans in her later life with her hardline views on immigration. Bardot was convicted five times for hate speech, particularly about Muslims, and up until her death she expressed her pleasure at the rising share of the vote gained by the anti-immigration National Rally party.
The proceeds from the auction will go to her animal welfare foundation and to Nicolas-Jacques Charrier, her only child.

Founded by the actor in 1986, the Brigitte Bardot Foundation says it has taken in 13,000 animals through four shelters and 150 partner facilities, supports 350 groups in France and operates in 70 countries.
About 3,000 French and international bidders registered for the auction.
“Brigitte Bardot has once again proved to be a remarkable alchemist: she transformed about €50,000 in estimates into nearly €1m, including fees,” the auctioneer Alexandre Millon said.
Two dog collars, with an ID tag bearing Bardot’s name and a telephone number, estimated at €30 for the pair, sold for €9,400 to a Russian buyer.

blocks.caption: Bardot’s widower has said her belongings should have been preserved as part of her legacy. Photograph: Urman Lionel/ABACA/Shutterstock

blocks.text: A self-portrait fetched nearly €40,000 while the typewriter she used to write an autobiography raised €4,634.
Estimated at between €300 and €500, two of her guitars soared to €8,600 and €1,900, while three stuffed toys representing baby seals sold for nearly €2,200.

“This sale is the logical continuation of the one she herself organised in 1987 with her most precious belongings to create her foundation,” Ghyslaine Calmels-Bock, the managing director of the Bardot Foundation, told AFP after the sale. “Today, her fight continues through this auction.”
Two days before the auction Bardot’s last husband, Bernard d’Ormale, deescribed it as a “joke”.
“These are personal items,” he said. “Why hold this sale? For the animals?” He said it amounted to a “disrespect to Brigitte’s memory”.
Her belongings should have been preserved as part of her legacy, he told AFP, adding that Bardot “would not have agreed to this sale”.
The foundation rejected the criticism, saying the auction had been approved by the board in June when the widower was its president.
D’Ormale said he had not understood the auction would involve such personal items.
The dispute comes days after he was removed as head of the foundation, a role he had held since Bardot’s death.

articles.title: Philippines, EU move closer to a free-trade agreement after decade of talks
articles.summary: Negotiators were instructed to finalize the agreement as soon as possible.

blocks.text: September 22, 2026 | 2:48pm

In this composite image, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., left, speaks at a Foreign Correspondents' Association of the Philippines forum in Manila on Aug. 14, 2026, while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen delivers an address at the European Parliament in Strasbourg, France, on Sept. 16, 2026.
AFP / Ted Aljibe and Jean-Christophe Verhaegen

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines and the European Union have reached "substantial agreement" on a free-trade pact after a decade of stop-start negotiations, putting the long-sought deal within reach of a possible signing in 2027.
The agreement is not finished, however, and negotiators must settle the remaining details before the pact can move through formal approval, signature and ratification procedures.
Trade Secretary Cristina Roque and EU Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maroš Šef?ovi? instructed their negotiating teams to finalize the agreement "as soon as possible."

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, following a separate call with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., said the two sides were "about to conclude talks." She said she looked forward to returning to the Philippines in 2027 to sign the agreement.

The proposed Philippines-EU Free Trade Agreement would cover tariffs on goods as well as services, investment, government procurement, digital trade, intellectual property and other rules governing cross-border business.
Both sides expect the pact to deepen trade and investment ties, diversify supply chains and give companies more predictable access to each other's markets.
Beyond GSP+
The EU is already one of the Philippines' largest economic partners.

Two-way trade in goods reached €17.6 billion in 2025, making the EU the Philippines' fourth-largest trading partner and accounting for 8.3% of its total goods trade, according to European Commission data.
Trade in services totaled €10.3 billion in 2024, while the stock of EU foreign direct investment in the Philippines stood at €15.4 billion.
Philippine exporters already enjoy preferential access to the European market through the EU's Generalised Scheme of Preferences Plus, or GSP+.

The program grants zero tariffs on roughly two-thirds of EU product categories, subject to the Philippines' continued compliance with international conventions on human and labor rights, environmental protection and good governance.
An FTA would eventually replace that unilateral arrangement with a reciprocal framework negotiated by both sides.
For Philippine exporters, the deal could provide more predictable access to a market of more than 400 million consumers and potentially broader tariff and non-tariff advantages than GSP+ offers.
European companies, meanwhile, are seeking greater access to the Philippine market and clearer rules for investment and government procurement.

Roque and Šef?ovi? said the agreement would create opportunities for businesses, including micro, small and medium enterprises, farmers and manufacturers. They also cited more diversified supply chains as a strategic benefit amid geopolitical and economic uncertainty.
A decade of talks
The Philippines and the EU launched free-trade negotiations in 2015 but held only two rounds before talks stalled in 2017.
Technical stocktaking—a form of preliminary review—began in 2023, followed by the formal resumption of negotiations in March 2024. Six negotiating rounds were held through May 2026.
Once the remaining issues are settled, the pact must still clear legal and political procedures before it can take effect.

Von der Leyen described the prospective deal as part of the EU's broader push for deeper economic ties with Southeast Asia. The bloc views bilateral agreements with individual ASEAN economies as building blocks toward stronger region-to-region trade ties.

articles.title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial Day 27: Records showed VP Sara retained business interests, corporate positions
articles.summary: On the 27th day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, the exchange included that she allegedly held a directorship position and was a shareholder in a private business from 2016 up…

blocks.text: On the 27th day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, the exchange included that she allegedly held a directorship position and was a shareholder in a private business from 2016 up to 2025 and that the subpoena for Davao City Mayor Sebastian "Baste" Duterte was recalled.

This was because the prosecution witness SEC Company Registration and Monitoring Department Director Gerardo Fernando Del Rosario testified on the corporate records of the 18 companies which either the Vice President or her husband, Atty. Manases Carpio, owns or have business interest in.

Defense counsel Justin Gular was quick to move for the exclusion and discussion of corporate documents belonging to JTC Group of Companies and Pikimong Pikimong Philippines Corporation, citing such companies were not covered by the subpoena issued by the Senate impeachment court.
The court ruled in favor of Gular.

Del Rosario then said the Vice President is prohibited to participate in any business activity during her tenure as Vice President as provided under Article 7, Section 13 of the Constitution which reads “The President and Vice President shall not, during said tenure, directly or indirectly, practice any other profession, participate in any business, or be financially interested in any contract with, or in any franchise, or special privilege granted by the government or any subdivision, agency, or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries.”

Likewise, Del Rosario testified that the Vice President did not relinquish her post as one of the Board of Directors of Metro City Chow Foods Corporation since she assumed office as Vice President in June 30, 2022 despite the Constitutional prohibition.

Based on SEC records, Del Rosario said the Vice President was still listed as Metro City Chow Foods Corporation’s Director in the company’s 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 General Information Sheet findings.
But as to the 18 firms, Del Rosario said that 10 did not declare dividends in multiple years covering years 2004 to 2025.
These 10 include:

items: City Hall King Chow Foods Corporation
Metro City Chow Foods Corporation
Gencorp Industries, Inc.
Cale88 Foods Corporation
Mati City Ice Plant & Cold Storage
Davao Emerging Taipans Corporation
Geometry Security and Investigation Agency, Inc.
3Kids Trucking Services, Inc.
CYK&T Davao Corporation
SGT Fortune Horse Corporation

blocks.text: On the other hand, the eight of the 18 did not submit any annual financial statement.
These eight, on the other hand, are:

items: Davao Bounty Times Foods Corp.
Madayaw fisheries Inc.
Great Jolly Times Food Corp.
Amianan Shores Inc.
Timesqure Bee Foods Corp.
Cabletow 88 Shipping and Marine Services, Inc.
Davao New Royal Taipan Foods Corporation
Carpio Lawyers

blocks.text: With no financial statement, Del Rosario said there is no basis to determine if these eight companies had paid dividends to its stockholders or otherwise.

Before the trial day ended, that the Senate impeachment court has recalled the subpoena for the Vice President’s younger brother, Davao City Mayor Sebastian "Baste" Duterte and two others to appear on September 23, Wednesday, when oral arguments on the voting threshold have been scheduled.
As a result, the younger Duterte’s expected appearance has been moved between September 28 to 30.

The testimony of the Davao City mayor was sought by the prosecutors since he was listed as one of the officials of Gencorp Industries, Inc. which was one the businesses that the Vice President declared under her SALN.

GenCorp’s corporate records do not show the Vice President as one of its incorporators or directors, but the Vice President declared it as one of her business interests in her SALN as Vice President in 2024 and 2025.
This discrepancy in declaration and the absence or lack of dividends paid by the 18 firms, the prosecution panel said, puts the credibility of the Vice President’s SALN declaration questionable.

In a separate press conference, defense counsel Michael Poa said he won’t advise the Vice President to attend her impeachment trial in person, saying that such decision only lies with the Vice President.

Before the trial started, the House prosecution panel on Monday decided to forgo presenting Assistant Commissioner Ariel Ronquillo of the Civil Service Commission as a witness for the impeachment trial of Vice President Duterte.

House prosecutor Terry Ridon said this was because the prosecution was already satisfied with the testimony of former Sandiganbayan Presiding Justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang and Atty. Karen Batu of the Office of the Ombudsman who testified on anti-corruption and SALN laws, respectively. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Cybersecurity agency directs Discord, Reddit to set up Philippine offices
articles.summary: Reddit and Discord were also directed by the CICC to submit a written explanation of their existing safety and age verification measures.

blocks.text: Headlines
September 22, 2026 | 2:39pm
This composite shows the online community platforms Reddit and Discord.
AFP / Kirill Kudryavtsev; Mauro Pimentel

MANILA, Philippines — Online community platforms Discord and Reddit have been directed to establish their own offices in the Philippines as local authorities continue to examine the spread of violent ideologies online.

The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) said Tuesday, September 22, that they have sent separate letters to the executives of the two platforms demanding their immediate presence in the country.

The letters, dated September 21, pressed the two platforms to set up an office and to designate a resident agent or local representative who can coordinate with the Philippine authorities within 24 hours after their receipt of the letter.

“We are not asking platforms to police the internet for the government but to be reachable, accountable, and responsive when activities on their platforms put Filipino children and communities at risk,” the CICC said.
Digital exploitation of minors
The move came following the school shooting incident in South Cotabato on September 18, which is the third recorded incident of a school shooting in the country involving students as shooters.

The alleged suspect in the recent killing, who is a 16-year-old Grade 9 student, killed two of his classmates and himself using the handgun of his father, who works for the Department of Education (DepEd).
Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla earlier said that based on the initial police investigation, the suspect had access to the dark web.
Remulla then called for a total ban against websites and online platforms that promote violence and hate.

Meanwhile, the CICC said they are also seeking the two platforms’ cooperation in developing the proposed framework to combat online sexual abuse and exploitation of children (OSAEC), child sexual abuse or exploitation of materials (CSAEM), and nihilistic violent extremism (NVE).
Addressing online threats

The CICC also tapped the help of the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) in setting up a meeting with the executives of Discord, Reddit and Meta to address other forms of “online threats linked to violence and the exploitation of children”.

The Philippine government had earlier met with executives from Meta and Roblox late in August to discuss the implementation of child safety measures and to establish their respective local offices as well.
Reddit and Discord were also directed by the CICC to submit a written explanation of their existing safety and age verification measures.

“The CICC warned that failure or refusal to comply with the prescribed period could prompt the agency, in coordination with appropriate Philippine authorities, to restrict their operations or prohibit access of users to the platforms in the Philippines,” the agency said.

articles.title: DILG revises approval process for local officials' foreign travel
articles.summary: The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) on Tuesday said it has revised the approval process for foreign travel requests of local government officials.

blocks.text: Published September 22, 2026 2:34pm
The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) on Tuesday said it has revised the approval process for foreign travel requests of local government officials.

Under the new process, the DILG Secretary still approves travel for certain high-level officials and certain circumstances. But the authority for other cases is delegated to DILG Regional, Provincial, and City Directors.

“Administrative Order No. 47, s. 2026 authorizes the DILG Secretary to further delegate the approval of foreign travel requests of local officials and employees. Previously, the authority delegated by the President rested with the DILG Secretary,” the Department said.

Under DILG Circular No. 2026-017, the Secretary remains the approving authority for all official and unofficial foreign travel of Provincial Governors, Highly Urbanized City and Independent Component City (HUC/ICC) Mayors, and the Municipal Mayor of Pateros.
The DILG said the Secretary will approve foreign travel of provincial, city, and municipal elective officials if the trip exceeds three months or takes place during an emergency or crisis.

But for official trips lasting three months or less and when there is no emergency or crisis, DILG Regional Directors may approve the foreign travel of provincial, city, and municipal elective officials.

Regional Directors will also decide on foreign travel requests of appointive officials and employees of provinces, cities, and municipalities when the trip is more than three months or takes place during an emergency or crisis.

Meanwhile, for barangays in component cities and municipalities, DILG Provincial Directors will approve official and unofficial foreign travel of elective and appointive officials when the trip exceeds three months or occurs during an emergency or crisis.
But for barangays in HUCs and ICCs, foreign travel requests under the same circumstances will be handled by the DILG City Director.
The DILG continues to process applications through its Foreign Travel Authority Online System (FTA OS), where applicants may submit the required documents electronically.
The revised approval mechanism took effect on September 7, 2026. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: ‘What we have is unique’: the Indian craftsmanship behind global luxury fashion
articles.summary:
Generations of artisans from Mumbai to Lucknow have shaped the world’s most coveted designs. Plus, the gen Z memes giving classic Bollywood a new life

The

blocks.text: The zardozi embroidery on a Dior dress, the T-strap leather sandals at a Prada show, the mirror-work technique used on a Fendi bag – for decades, the skill of Indian artisans has been an invisible force behind some of the world’s most coveted fashion.
Now, that work is beginning to claim its own place in the spotlight, and the Mumbai-based textile and embroidery atelier Chanakya International is at the forefront.

Chanakya marked its 40th anniversary this month, celebrating with three exhibitions that trace its journey from an embroidery powerhouse to a present-day craft and cultural institution. The person steering it is 49-year-old Karishma Swali, whose father set up the group’s operations in the 1980s.

“What we have as a country is unique,” she tells me of India’s rich textile and craft heritage. “It’s unparalleled in many ways, and it’s the only place where we continue to practise it.” During the Renaissance, she says, France and Italy had established and varied traditions. “But what we have in India today is [what] other parts of the world have lost.”

Chanakya has a network of 1,400 artisans, and says that some are 13th-generation craftspeople, skilled in hundreds of embroidery traditions and supplying almost every luxury label you can imagine. Among the techniques they have revived is the Mughal-era silver filigree lace, or chaand jaal, reintroduced in a lighter form that has since become a regular feature in couture collections.

In 2023, Dior held a show at Mumbai’s Gateway of India, showcasing its partnership with Chanakya, in a high-profile acknowledgment of Indian craftsmanship. The runway saw sari-inspired skirts, vibrant madras-checks sets and Nehru-collar jackets.

These collaborations are supported by expert craft knowledge passed down and refined over generations, and they need institutional support to survive. The Kalhath Institute, a craft-preservation centre in Lucknow, runs residencies that pair artists from across the world with local artisans.

Kalhath’s co-founder Mohammed Amine Dadda tells me that Indian craftsmanship’s defining quality is “intelligence of the hand” – a sensitive, slow and cumulative process underpinned by patience and dexterity. “Without this technical mastery, and the considerable time required to create the most demanding pieces, haute couture and contemporary luxury simply could not bring their most ambitious creative visions to life.”

This mastery is not limited to textiles. When it comes to jewellery, global luxury brands have long sought Jaipur-based the Gem Palace, established in 1852 by the Kasliwal family, who still run it today. Samarth Kasliwal, 33, says part of the appeal lies in the visual language of Indian artistry itself. “There is something about Indian artistry that is inspired by nature,” he tells me, pointing to the recurring use of floral patterns and animals across Indian art and design. These motifs are universal, and travel across the lines of culture and language.

One recent collaboration Kasliwal is particularly proud of is a collection for Dior featuring green onyx and rock crystals, with engravings of birds, animals and flowers. The combination, he says, is reminiscent of traditional Indian jewellery, while drawing on techniques that remain central to the atelier’s work today.

blocks.caption: Jaipur-based Gem Palace has worked with the French fashion house Dior on a jewellery collection. Photograph: Courtesy of Gem Palace and Dior

blocks.text: With increased visibility, the question of credit and appropriation has become harder to ignore. Last week, a Ralph Lauren gown from the designer’s spring 2027 collection attracted criticism after many Indians pointed out that the embroidery the brand described as “embellishments” looked a lot like Indian zardozi, but without any accompanying credit. (Ralph Lauren did not respond to my request for comment.)

Then, Fendi came under fire when people noticed that a baguette bag from its autumn/winter collection featured mirrorwork often seen in Gujarati crafts. In April, Fendi credited Chanakya artisans in a social media video showcasing the same embroidery. But the product description on its site failed to mention any Indian inspiration, and its final label read “Made in Italy”.

After I asked Fendi about the discrepancy, the brand cited its “creative partnership” with Chanakya of more than three decades, saying it “remains committed to supporting and recognizing India’s rich craft heritage”. The website descriptor now reads: “Made in Italy and India with Chanakya”.
A recent Financial Times report noted that under EU rules, garments embroidered in India can still end up with a European label – so long as the final construction and finishing take place in Europe.

Last year, Prada was accused of appropriating Indian culture with Kolhapuri-inspired sandals, a controversy that showed us these debates around recognition can sometimes produce a more structural response. “We acknowledge the sandals … are inspired by traditional Indian handcrafted footwear, with a centuries-old heritage,” Lorenzo Bertelli, the corporate social responsibility chief at the Italian fashion house, had written in a letter to the Maharashtra chamber of commerce at the time.

Prada subsequently partnered with state-backed organisations in Maharashtra and Karnataka to produce a limited-edition collection, Made in India, and committed to a three-year training programme for artisans specialising in the craft.

blocks.caption: Karishma Swali with Chanakya School of Craft students. Photograph: Hashim Badani/ Chanakya International

blocks.text: Might these collaborations, controversies and corrections represent a shift in India’s place in the fashion industry? Anthropologist Phyllida Jay, author of Inspired by India: How India Transformed Global Design, appears to think so, placing the debate in a longer arc. “The stories of the ateliers producing highly skilled Indian craft in the elevated realm of European luxury and high fashion is part of a broader paradigm shift,” she writes, “where over 70 years after the end of colonial rule, India is being looked at in a different way on the world stage.” It is, in a way, a reversal, moving from a colonial history of extraction toward one in which Indians themselves get a voice in how their craft is represented.

Swali is ensuring this visibility also lives on through the Chanakya School of Craft, which she set up in 2016. Its 18-month programme provides free embroidery training and a travel honorarium to dozens of women, some of whom have gone on to work at the main atelier. Others have set up their own independent studios.

I had a chance to visit the space – inside a high-rise in Lower Parel, where those as young as 18 learn intricate needlework alongside grandmothers in their 60s. “Craft in India has never been institutionalised,” Swali says of the ethos behind the initiative. “It’s intergenerational,” she says, adding that women have often been excluded.

India’s culture of craft has always been precious. Growing up, I loved having the choice to affordably create any type of clothing. At one point, I had a small army of tailors, each with a different specialisation, whom I’d go to for different needs. I’d buy ajrakh and mashru silks from Dastkar or Nalli, and hand it to the right Masterji to stitch, embroider and tweak to my size. So, to me, Indian craftsmanship is not just a part of luxury, but a luxury itself.
What else we’re reading about

blocks.caption: Time Out has named Mumbai’s Bandra West one of the coolest neighbourhoods in the world. Photograph: Danto Production

blocks.text: Travel | Time Out just confirmed what everyone in Mumbai’s Bandra West knows: that it’s one of the coolest neighbourhoods in the world. The other Indian spot to make the cut is Delhi’s food and fashion centre, Humayunpur. The top spot went to Jongno 3-ga in Seoul – my second home!
after newsletter promotion

Business | India will levy a 0.4% charge on merchants for UPI payments above Rs 2,000, starting on 15 October. The charges will not be applicable when the payment is made from one person to another. Ashneer Grover, co-founder and former CEO of fintech firm BharatPe slammed the move, describing it as “tax collection”.

Immigration | An investigation by Scroll’s Rokibuz Zaman has revealed a troubling pattern in West Bengal: since June, at least nine Muslim men and two children have been picked up by the police from their homes over allegations that they are Bangladeshi nationals – without being given a chance to prove their citizenship. Most were picked up and detained in midnight raids, the report said, and family members accused the police of not producing warrants.
Guest shelf
A recommendation from someone with great taste

blocks.caption: Fashion designer Payal Khandwala recommends the perfect saree weave. Photograph: Payal Khandwala

blocks.text: Fashion designer Payal Khandwala, whose spring-summer ’26 collection featured handwoven silks, cottons and brocades, recommends the perfect saree weave: “The delicate poetry of a Jamdani saree is definitely my favourite. A 2,000-year-old craft, typically woven in fine muslin and of Bengali origin, it’s somewhat an unsung hero. The weaving process itself is exceptionally intricate. Using a supplementary weft technique, thousands of markings are meticulously mapped on to the warp to recreate the pattern, interlaced by hand with a wooden shuttle and metallic needle to guide the motifs in silver and gold yarn, on fine mulberry silk and organza.”
Count it
A number worth knowing

blocks.caption: Foreign portfolio investors have pulled out £1.2bn from Indian equities. Photograph: Francis Mascarenhas/Reuters

blocks.text: Foreign investors have pulled out Rs 13,138 crore (£1.02bn) from Indian equities in the first half of September, wiping out about half of the net inflows recorded in August.
Vibe check

blocks.caption: Old Bollywood, new jokes … the memes giving classic film stills a gen Z makeover. Photograph: Bahaish Kapoor

blocks.text: The true measure of my love for my friends is in the number of memes I send them. One of the accounts I rely on is Bahaish Kapoor’s. The screenwriter-turned-meme evangelist pairs black-and-white Bollywood stills with contemporary gen Z sass, and lets incongruity do the rest. What makes an image meme-worthy? “I always look for people who are in a deep philosophical, romantic, dramatic action moment which I can repurpose to bring in a whole new meaning,” he tells me. “I try to mix and match and see what’s working.” His 340,000-plus followers include Sharon Stone and Hrithik Roshan.

“I just want to make people feel a little better,” says Kapoor, adding that he receives a lot of DMs from people about how his page helped them through a bad day. “People confessing that they are lighter because of this experience is all that I can hope for. I mean, that’s the endgame.”
