articles.title: Who is Rendell Sopeña?
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel on Tuesday presented Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS) Division Chief Rendell Sopeña as a witness in the impeachment trial of Vice President…

blocks.text: Published September 22, 2026 2:13pm

The House prosecution panel on Tuesday presented Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS) Division Chief Rendell Sopeña as a witness in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
During direct examination by lead Prosecutor Gerville Luistro, Sopeña said he heads the Electronic Government Procurement Operations Division (EGPOD) of PhilGEPS.

“It is the division under the PhilGEPS office that has sole custody of the PhilGEPS System database. The division also processes procurement requests from internal and external stakeholders,” he said.
Sopeña said he became division chief in March 2025.
“As division chief of EGPOD, I am the one who manages everything. And I am the overall custodian of the PhilGEPS System database,” he said.
“In line with this, I am the one who issues certificates upon the request of internal stakeholders and in response to subpoenas and request letters received by the PhilGEPS Office,” he added.
As division chief, Sopeña said he also validates requested data and issues certifications based on such requests.
Before joining EGPOD, Sopeña said he was an information technology officer at the Armed Forces of the Philippines Retirement and Separation Benefits System.

Sopeña is testifying as a prosecution witness on Duterte’s alleged corporate ownership and shareholdings in connection with Article 2 of the impeachment complaint, which accuses her of accumulating unexplained wealth.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Prosecution: Baste Duterte's statement on GenCorp 'a confession of sins'
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel said Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte"s statement that the Davao City government inked P33 million worth of contracts with Gencorp. Industries Inc. is a confession.

blocks.text: SARA DUTERTE IMPEACHMENT TRIAL
Published September 22, 2026 2:03pm

Private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan was referring to Mayor Duterte’s statement that the Davao City government's transactions with GenCorp. reached over P33.2 million across 19 contracts, that these are all above board, and that himself and the rest of Davao city government officials “never had any knowledge of Vice President Sara Duterte holding an interest in “Gencorp. Industries Inc.”

Vice President Sara Duterte, who is facing an impeachment trial, declared GenCorp. Industries Inc. as one of her business interests in her 2024 and 2025 Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth.

The Vice President’s name, however, is not found on GenCorp.’s corporate records submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) as testified by SEC Company Registration and Monitoring Department Director Gerardo del Rosario.
“In fact, para maintindihan ng publiko, confession ‘yan. Parang free spirited,” Kapunan told reporters during Day 28 of the impeachment trial of the Vice President.
(For the public to understand, that is a confession. It was free-spirited.)
“What do you do when you confess to the priest? You admit to your sins, right? This is not only an admission. This is also a confession,” Kapunan added.
The Senate impeachment court has issued an order for Mayor Duterte to testify before the impeachment trial of his sister, Vice President Duterte, due to their links to GenCorp.
This court order was issued on the request of the prosecution.

Private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr., for his part, said Mayor Duterte’s statement is welcome but maintained he should still face the impeachment court for his remarks to be entered into the records of the Senate impeachment trial proceedings.

“GenCorp. is in the SALN of the Vice President, she has financial interest there [as she stated in her SALN]. Now, he said himself that the Davao city entered into transactions with GenCorp., and that it is worth P30 million. All the more that we want him to take the witness stand to put those [statements] on record for the Senate impeachment court to appreciate,” Tolosa said.
“We’ll need that [on record] for the impeachment court to decide,” Tolosa added.
Kapunan, however, stopped short of saying that Mayor Duterte's 'confession' will boost their impeachment case against the Vice President.

"I rest my case. That's already [calling for] an opinion. I don't have P30,000 with me at the moment," she added, referring to the fine to those who will violate the ban on the parties from speaking on the merits of the impeachment case under Rule 18 of the Senate impeachment rules or sub judice rule. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Texas ICE shooting leaves Venezuelan DoorDash driver with bullet in his back, says lawyer
articles.summary: The delivery driver was transferred from a hospital to a detention centre, his lawyer tells US media.

blocks.text: Attorney Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch told CBS that Garcés Perez called his wife while "yelling in pain" in hospital. She told National Public Radio he was in ICE custody.
The Trump administration has ramped up immigration enforcement efforts and arrests during Trump's second term, sparking unrest across several US cities.

The administration has defended its policies and the agency's controversial tactics as necessary for public safety and to enact Trump's campaign promise to secure the border and carry out mass deportations.
The shooting in Austin on Sunday occurred just before 1300 local time, although details remain scarce.
Dozens of protesters, some waving the flags of Mexico and Guatemala, gathered at the scene carrying signs demanding that ICE leave Austin.

Local television outlets showed the demonstrators gathering across the street from ​a blue Toyota Corolla that ⁠sustained damage to the passenger-side door, as ICE agents stood nearby, Reuters news agency reported.
Mayor Kirk Watson, a Democrat, said that Austinites have a right to know what happened and "a right to feel safe in their city" during a media briefing on Sunday.
"They should know the truth," he said, adding that he is pleased that the city will also be involved in the investigation.
He added that ICE operations have surged in Austin in recent weeks.
ICE has faced intense scrutiny after a number of deadly shootings, including the death of Houston resident Lorenzo Salgado Araujo.
Salgado Araujo had not been a target of an ICE investigation, but was shot during an ICE traffic stop, according to DHS.

Texas Congressman Greg Casar, a Democrat, has demanded a full and immediate independent investigation into the latest shooting and the release of body camera footage. He also demanded "accountability for any ICE officer who broke the law".
Activists say that the administration has violated due process as it carries out the crackdown.
Democrats have demanded reforms at the agency, including requiring immigration enforcement agents to wear body cameras and not conceal their faces.

Earlier this month the US Department of Justice charged an ICE agent with lying about the non-fatal shooting of a Venezuelan migrant in Minnesota - a rare instance in which the current justice department accused a federal agent of breaking the law on the job.

Earlier this week, Florida lawmaker Maria Elvira Salazar, a Republican who has spoken out against the immigration crackdown, released an advert criticising the targeting and detaining of individuals who have no criminal record.
Salazar appeared on the CBS programme Face the Nation on Sunday and said that she has since spoken to the president, and believes he will keep the country on the right track.
"He gets it more than anybody," she said.

articles.title: PAGASA: LPA east of Philippines has ‘high chance’ of developing into tropical depression
articles.summary: According to PAGASA, as of 10 a.m., the LPA is estimated to be 1,760 kilometers east of Eastern Visayas.

blocks.text: September 22, 2026 | 1:52pm
Satellite image from PAGASA showing the low-pressure area east of the Philippines as of 8 a.m. on Sept. 22, 2026.
PAGASA / Released
MANILA, Philippines — A low pressure area (LPA) located east of the Philippines has a high chance of developing into a tropical depression, the state weather bureau PAGASA said.
According to PAGASA, as of 8 a.m., the LPA was estimated to be 1,760 kilometers east of Eastern Visayas, although the information was posted only at 10 a.m.
It was moving north-northwestward at 15 kilometers per hour.
On Tuesday, September 22, PAGASA said the LPA's trough is expected to bring cloudy skies with scattered rain and thunderstorms over Eastern Visayas, Caraga, Bohol and Davao Oriental.

However, Palawan, Occidental Mindoro and Oriental Mindoro may experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rain showers or thunderstorms due to the southwest monsoon, locally known as “habagat.”
Meanwhile, Metro Manila and the rest of the country may experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rain showers or thunderstorms due to localized thunderstorms.

articles.title: Iran must stop arming Houthis in Yemen, G7 says ahead of UN General Assembly
articles.summary: The G7 also condemns "in the strongest terms" Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, saying that the escalation in fighting in Yemen jeopardises global energy security.

blocks.text: Iran must "end its arming of and support" for the Houthis in Yemen, the foreign ministers of G7 nations have said in a joint statement.

The G7 also condemned "in the strongest terms" Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, adding that the recent escalation in fighting against Saudi-backed forces in Yemen represented a threat to regional and global energy security.

Thousands of refugees have fled Yemen in recent days after the Iran-backed group seized territory along the country's Red Sea coastline, including near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a critical shipping route for global trade.
The statement comes ahead of the annual UN General Assembly in New York, where senior Iranian officials are due to speak.

"We call on the Houthis to immediately cease all military actions, all threats and attacks against civilian shipping, and to return to the political process in good faith," said the foreign ministers of the UK, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.

It went on: "Their reprehensible actions constitute a dangerous pattern of escalation that risks further exacerbating the conflict, undermining international trade and creating global economic instability."

"Looking forward, we will continue to support the legitimate Government of Yemen and reaffirm our strong commitment to the unity, sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of Yemen," the ministers said.
Their statement was issued following a meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.
Saudi Arabia has retaliated with hundreds of air strikes in the region.
The Houthis have also launched hundreds of drones and missiles at cities and infrastructure in south-western Saudi Arabia, including the capital city, Riyadh.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said the UK will provide "defensive air-to-air refuelling" support for Saudi Arabia, involving a single British aircraft, a Voyager, based out of RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus.
Burnham said the announcement followed a request from Saudi Arabia for "military support", which he agreed to on the advice of Defence Secretary Wes Streeting and Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband.
A diplomatic source told AFP that France has pledged support as well, and says is ready to work on "securing" Saudi energy infrastructure via a "strictly defensive approach".
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has also requested military support from President Donald Trump, US media reported.
Trump has wavered for weeks over whether to act on a Saudi request for help in fighting the Houthis, the New York Times reported on Monday.
The US president had earlier told Fox News that he was in "deciding mode" as he considered options for the next steps in the war against Iran.
On Sunday, US embassies across the Middle East issued new security alerts as fighting between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed coalition in Yemen intensified.
The Houthis declare themselves to be part of the Iranian-led "axis of resistance" against Israel, the US and the wider West - along with armed group such as Hamas and Lebanon's Hezbollah movement.
Tehran has previously denied supplying weapons to the Houthis and says it only supports them politically.

articles.title: Outrage in India over viral video of teen molested and her friend beaten
articles.summary: Three minors were arrested after videos capturing the assault went viral in India, sparking anger.

blocks.text: A video showing a teenaged girl being sexually assaulted and her male friend beaten by a group of men in India's Bihar state has sparked widespread outrage.
The school students, both minors, were stopped in Jamui district on 19 September. Footage shared widely online shows them surrounded and repeatedly pleading to be allowed to leave.
The boy is seen being slapped and pulled by his collar, while the girl is touched inappropriately and, in another clip, carried away by a man as the boy tries to intervene.
Three accused, also minors, have been arrested in connection with the assault. A special investigation team has been set up to catch the other suspects.

The disturbing footage has prompted anger over the harassment of the two teenagers and renewed a wider debate about the safety of women and girls in Bihar, as well as questions over the response of state authorities.
The outrage intensified after Bihar minister Shravan Kumar said that "sporadic incidents keep happening" and that the government was keeping a watch on them.
"The world is not entirely free of crime," he said, adding that those responsible would not be allowed to escape and would face strict action.

Umesh Kushwaha, of the governing Janata Dal (United), also faced criticism after referring to such cases as "isolated incidents" and contrasting the government's record with that of the previous RJD administration.
Kushwaha later said his remarks had been "distorted and misrepresented" and promised action against those responsible.
Police said the incident took place around 19:00 local time [13:30 GMT] on Saturday, but it came to light on Monday after the video of the assault went viral.
The teenagers, both students of 10th standard, attended the same coaching institute and had gone to the area to take photographs after their classes, according to police.

Jamui police chief Bishwajeet Dayal said neither of them had initially reported the incident - officers began investigating after the video circulated widely online and traced the pair using the registration number of a vehicle visible in the footage.
Their statements were subsequently recorded and a case was registered following a written complaint from the girl.
A case has been registered under India's stringent Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, or Pocso.

Police have also invoked sections of India's criminal code covering assault or criminal force against a woman with intent to outrage her modesty, assault or criminal force with intent to disrobe, and acts carried out with a common intention.
Senior police officer KS Anupam said three minors had been arrested and that investigators had established the involvement of two other people.
Police have also begun action against 32 social media accounts accused of circulating footage in which the teenagers could be identified, she added.

The shocking nature of the assault has provoked outrage online, with many social media users expressing horror and questioning why a group of men believed they had the right to confront two teenagers for being together.
Some characterised the incident as an extreme form of "moral policing", while others tagged Bihar police and demanded strict action against the harassers.
Shreyasi Singh, a Bihar minister and legislator from Jamui, told NDTV news channel, external the incident had brought "shame to society".
Singh, a former international-level sport shooter, said women in Bihar were advancing in many areas but concerns about their safety persisted.
She called for the remaining suspects to be arrested quickly and for strict action against those responsible.
Opposition leaders, meanwhile, have seized on the case to question the state government's record on women's safety.

Rahul Gandhi, MP and senior leader of India's main opposition Congress party, described the footage as "deeply disturbing" and said the incident reflected a patriarchal "belief that men could police a girl's body, movements and choices".
"This is not culture. It is patriarchy," Gandhi wrote on X (formerly Twitter).
Tejashwi Yadav, the opposition leader in Bihar, said the incident had left him "deeply ashamed" and accused the government of failing to ensure the safety of women and girls in the state.
Members of Bihar's governing coalition have rejected the opposition's wider criticism of the state's law-and-order record and said those responsible for the attack would face strict action.
India's National Commission for Women has also intervened, calling for all those involved to be identified and arrested and for an impartial investigation.
The commission has asked for a report from Bihar police and urged authorities to prevent further sharing of the video clips to protect the girl's identity and privacy.
The Bihar State Women's Commission has also sought information from district authorities about the action being taken in the case.

articles.title: G7 demands Houthis 'immediately' cease Saudi strikes
articles.summary: The G7 nations have accused Yemen's Houthi rebels of targeting civilian shipping near Saudi Arabia. UK PM Andy Burnham said he will offer "time-limited" and "defensive" military support to repel the…

image.caption: Yemen's Houthi rebels recently claimed responsibility for a September 19 attack on Riyadh AirportImage: REUTERS

blocks.text: The foreign ministers of G7 nations on Monday denounced Houthi attacks in Yemen and against Saudi Arabia while urging Iran to end its support, including arming, of the rebels,

"We condemn in ‌the strongest terms the unacceptable continued strikes carried out by ‌the Houthis in Yemen ‌and against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," the ministers of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States said in a joint statement, after meeting on the sidelines of the UNGA.
The statement called on the Houthis to "immediately cease all military actions, all threats and attacks against civilian shipping, and to return to the political process in good faith."
UK offers air-to-air refuelling assistance to Saudi aircraft
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has agreed to give limited military support to Saudi Arabia as the Middle Eastern kingdom continues to face attacks from Yemen's Houthi rebels.

Britain's Royal Air Force (RAF) will provide "defensive" air-to-air refuelling for Saudi aircraft, Burham told reporters on Monday as he travelled to New York for the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).
The prime minister said that the UK had "received a request" from Saudi Arabia for military support.

The British leader said he was "acting to secure the interests of Britain and the wider region, because of course Saudi Arabia has been experiencing attack, is looking at potential further disruption, and we need to keep those pathways [for oil] open."
What do we know about the UK's 'defensive' military support to Saudi Arabia?
Reports cited UK officials as saying that the agreement, which is likely to start within days, will be time-capped and could last for "weeks".
The mission would involve the use of the RAF's Voyager tanker and is in addition to the UK Sky Sabre air defence system which is already deployed in Saudi Arabia.
The UK mission will support Saudi jets in defending the country from drone and missile attacks rather than supporting strikes against the Iran-backed Houthis, the PA news agency reported.
Escalating tensions between Houthis and Saudi Arabia
Since 2015, Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognized government in its fight against the Houthis.

In July this year, a 2022 truce between the rebels and Saudi Arabia crumbled after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen's capital Sanaa, which defied the Saudis' control over Yemeni airspace.
On Saturday, a Houthi attack on Riyadh was the first to target the Saudi capital in years.
The Houthis have also declared a blockade on Saudi shipping in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait — a crucial global shipping route — and the Red Sea.
Apart from Saudi-linked vessels, oil facilities inside Saudi Arabia — one of the world's top oil exporters — have also come under fire from Houthi drones and missiles.
Why can't Saudi Arabia stop the Houthis?

articles.title: 4 Russia-bound Filipinos recruited for military work stopped at NAIA
articles.summary: The bureau said they were recruited for security and military work in Russia.

blocks.text: September 22, 2026 | 12:50pm
Immigration gates at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport.
Bureau of Immigration Facebook page

MANILA, Philippines — Immigration officers at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal 1 intercepted four Filipinos whom the Bureau of Immigration said had been illegally recruited for security and military work in Russia.

The bureau said Tuesday, September 22, that the four were stopped in two separate incidents on September 18 and 19 after immigration officers noted inconsistencies in their statements during primary inspection.
On September 18, three male passengers identified only by the aliases "Aldo," 30; "Nery," 41; and "Baby," 38, attempted to board a flight to Thailand.
During secondary inspection, the three admitted that Russia, not Thailand, was their actual final destination, according to the bureau.
Aldo told immigration officers that he had been recruited through a Facebook post for a security job offering a monthly salary of P70,000.
Nery said he had been recruited by an unidentified individual in Bangkok, while Baby said his trip was sponsored by a contact identified only as "Alexander."

The following day, September 19, immigration officers intercepted another male passenger, identified as "King," 34, who declared Vietnam as his destination before boarding a Philippine Airlines flight.
During questioning, King admitted that he was actually bound for Russia after being recruited for military service, the immigration bureau said.
He was allegedly promised a monthly salary of P150,000, Russian citizenship after one year and additional bonuses for completing "special missions."
Immigration officers also recovered what the bureau described as a concealed Russian visa from alias King. He told officers that his recruiters had paid for all his travel expenses.
All four Filipinos were turned over to the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking for further investigation and assistance.
Recruitment patterns
Earlier this year, Philippine authorities warned Filipinos against overseas job offers linked to foreign armed forces, following reports of Filipinos being recruited into Russian military units.
In February, the Department of Foreign Affairs warned that such employment could expose Filipinos to "grave danger and serious legal consequences," including possible loss of citizenship.

In one earlier case, Filipino Raymon Gumangan said he traveled to Russia in 2024 for what had been presented as a logistics job but was instead assigned as a shooter in a Russian military parachute regiment. He was later captured in Ukraine in September 2025.

Ukrainian military intelligence also reported that another Filipino, identified only as "John Patrick," had been killed while serving with Russian forces in Donetsk, although Philippine authorities said at the time that they were still verifying the report.

articles.title: At least two people killed in Japan as typhoon Dujuan triggers heavy rain, landslides
articles.summary:
Storm triggers landslides and travel chaos while cutting off almost ‌50,000 homes from electricity

Typhoon Dujuan has killed at least two people in Japan, while tens of thousands of houses…

blocks.text: Typhoon Dujuan has killed at least two people in Japan, while tens of thousands of houses near Tokyo remained without power after the storm swept through the region, authorities said on Tuesday.
Dujuan – which brought violent winds of 144km/h (89mph) – was moving away from Japan on Tuesday morning, allowing authorities to downgrade most heavy rain and landslide warnings.

But the typhoon had already caused deaths, destruction and widespread chaos, including disruption of some events at the Asian Games and forcing the early closure in Tokyo of the one of the world’s biggest video game trade fairs.

The city of Yokosuka in Kanagawa prefecture, near Tokyo, reported multiple landslides because of the torrential rain. Mud flowing into a home killed a woman in her 60s in Yokosuka, the public ​broadcaster NHK said. Another person died in Chiba.

blocks.caption: Rescue workers search a house hit by a landslide triggered by Typhoon Dujuan in Miura, Japan. Photograph: KYODO/Reuters

blocks.text: Search operations were continuing for four people missing after the landslides, NHK said.
Almost ‌50,000 households ​were still ​without electricity in Chibam near Tokyo on Tuesday morning, officials said.
The storm forced Japan Airlines to cancel 135 flights and All Nippon Airways to scrap 140.
More than 1.6 million residents in and around Tokyo were urged to evacuate on Monday, according to the Fire and Disaster Management Agency. The evacuations were not mandatory.

blocks.caption: A boy cycles through a flooded street as Typhoon Dujuan brings heavy rain, in Ichikawa, in Chiba prefecture. Photograph: KYODO/Reuters

blocks.text: Although Dujuan weakened as it moved north-east, it dumped record rainfall in parts of the Tokyo area.
Oshima, an island about 120km south of central Tokyo, was drenched with 832mm of rain over 48 hours, more than double its average rainfall for the whole of September, NHK reported.
Rainfall in Tokyo’s Edogawa ward reached a record 282.5mm over 24 hours.

Japan often sees strong typhoons in the late summer and early autumn. But scientists say human-driven climate change is intensifying the risk posed by heavy rains because a warmer atmosphere holds more water.

Typhoon Dujuan is the latest extreme weather event in a ⁠year of unusually intense rain, floods and tropical ​cyclones that have hit ‌regions across ‌the globe, from east Asia to North America ‌and Europe.

Former Special Envoy to China Jaime T. Cruz, who served under former President Rodrigo Duterte, is the same person listed in the corporate records of firms linked to Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, the prosecution panel said Tuesday.

“Yes, Your Honor. Same name, same person,” Matib said.

Tulfo raised the issue while questioning prosecution witness lawyer Gerardo Del Rosario, director of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Company Registration and Monitoring Department, who was testifying on the corporate records of companies allegedly linked to Duterte and Carpio, including their incorporators, directors and shareholders.

items: City Hall King Chow Foods Corporation

articles.title: British Columbia sues OpenAI and Sam Altman over Tumbler Ridge mass school shooting
articles.summary:
Canadian province alleges deadly attack could have been prevented if company had warned police of shooter’s ChatGPT use

British Columbia has sued OpenAI in California, saying a mass shooting…

blocks.text: British Columbia has sued OpenAI in California, saying a mass shooting at a school in the province could have been prevented if the company had warned local ⁠law enforcement that the shooter ⁠had used ChatGPT to ​plan the massacre.

The lawsuit filed in San Francisco federal court on Monday names OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, as defendants. It is seeking damages to fund recovery efforts in the province after the February attack, as well as an order directing changes to the way the company handles ChatGPT conversations that could lead to violence.

Nine people, primarily children, were killed in the school shooting in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia. The shooter, Jesse Van ⁠Rootselaar, had been flagged by the company’s safety team after her conversations about gun violence, but the company did not alert police.

Altman published a letter ​to the community saying he was “deeply sorry” OpenAI had not contacted ‌law enforcement. He promised reforms, but never ‌followed through, despite efforts from British Columbia’s attorney general to engage, the lawsuit says.

The school where the shooting took place is in the process of being ‌demolished, and the province has been forced to absorb the costs of a replacement school, mental health care and other effects of the shooting, according to the lawsuit.

A spokesperson for OpenAI, Drew Pusateri, called the Tumbler Ridge shooting an unspeakable tragedy. “OpenAI remains committed to working collaboratively with government and law enforcement officials, and continuing to advance our ongoing safety work.”

British Columbia’s lawsuit comes after more than 30 family members of victims and others affected by the attack filed lawsuits in California, accusing the company of opting out of a chance to prevent ‌the shooting.

Van Rootselaar shot her mother and stepbrother at home before killing an educational assistant and five students aged 12 and 13 at her former school on 10 February, according to police. Van Rootselaar, who was 18, then died by ​suicide.

Van Rootselaar’s interactions with ChatGPT were first flagged by the company in June 2025. Safety team members recommended contacting police, but Altman and other OpenAI leadership overruled them, the lawsuit says, citing OpenAI whistleblowers who spoke to the Wall Street Journal in the wake of the shooting.
The shooter’s account was deactivated, but she was able to get a new account and continue using the platform to plan her attack.

After publication of the Wall Street Journal article, the company said the ⁠account was flagged by systems that identify “misuses of our models in furtherance of violent activities”, but the issues did ​not meet its internal criteria for reporting to law ​enforcement.

The lawsuit comes after a series of ​cases against OpenAI have been filed in US state and federal courts in recent months over claims ChatGPT facilitated violence, ​including lawsuits related to a mass ‌shooting at Florida State ​University last year.

In June, Florida became the ​first state to sue OpenAI over safety risks, accusing the company of misrepresenting the safety of its ChatGPT platform, which the lawsuit said had harmed children by providing information to school shooters, offering guidance on self-harm and addicting young users.

OpenAI, which has denied the claims, has said it trains its models to refuse requests that could “meaningfully enable violence”, and notifies law enforcement when conversations suggest “an imminent and credible risk of harm to others”.

articles.title: SEC witness: Ownership of shares evidence of business participation
articles.summary: House prosecution panel witness Gerardo del Rosario, director of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Company Registration and Monitoring Department, on Tuesday affirmed that the ownership of…

blocks.text: SARA DUTERTE IMPEACHMENT TRIAL
Published September 22, 2026 12:26pm

House prosecution panel witness Gerardo del Rosario, director of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Company Registration and Monitoring Department, on Tuesday affirmed that the ownership of shares is evidence of participation in a business.
In his interjection, Senator-Judge Raffy Tulfo questioned the witness if shares of stocks are considered securities and whether ownership of shares is evidence of participation.
Del Rosario answered, "Tama po (That's correct)."
He also affirmed that ownership of a share, regardless of the percentage, is evidence of participation.
"Opo (Yes), it constitutes ownership po," Del Rosario said.
Del Rosario said a government official such as the President and the Vice President cannot participate in any business under the 1987 Constitution.

Section 13 states: "The President, Vice-President, the Members of the Cabinet, and their deputies or assistants shall not… during said tenure, directly or indirectly, practice any other profession, participate in any business, or be financially interested in any contract with, or in any franchise, or special privilege granted by the Government or any subdivision, agency, or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries."
The witness previously testified that Duterte remained on the Board of Directors of Metro City Chow Foods Corporation until 2025 or even after she was elected and assumed office as Vice President.

Asked by private prosecutor Erwin Matib to explain what a board does, Del Rosario described its authority over the corporation's business and property, as well as its responsibilities to shareholders and government agencies.
On the board's role in conducting the company's business, Del Rosario replied, "Hindi po siya makakapag-conduct ng business kung wala po siyang Board of Directors."
(A firm cannot conduct business without a Board of Directors.)

Del Rosario is testifying as a prosecution witness on Duterte's alleged corporate ownership and shareholdings in connection with Article 2 of the impeachment complaint against Duterte, which accuses her of accumulating unexplained wealth. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: BOC files complaint with DOJ vs. 14 over misdeclared agri products
articles.summary: The Bureau of Customs on Tuesday filed a complaint with the Department of Justice against 14 individuals, including nine of its own personnel, over alleged misdeclared agricultural products at the…

blocks.text: Published September 22, 2026 11:48am

The Bureau of Customs (BOC) on Tuesday filed a complaint with the Department of Justice against 14 individuals, including nine of its own personnel, over alleged misdeclared agricultural products at the Port of Subic.

According to the BOC, six complaints were filed for alleged violation of the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act (CMTA) against the owner and representatives of Berches Consumer Goods Trading and the BOC personnel in charge of examining and appraising the goods.
BOC Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno said the respondents misdeclared white onions and carrots, totaling P17.5 million.
“Again, ito ay magsilbing babala kahit sa aming mga tauhan na mananagot ang mga nagkakamali sa batas,” he said.
(Again, this will serve as a warning, even to our personnel, that those who violate the law will be held accountable.)

“Ito ay utang natin sa ating mga kababayan, again mga magsasaka, mangingisda na naghihirap araw-araw upang kumita ng tama, magtrabaho nang marangal at itong mga smugglers ay hindi nahihiya sa kanilang patuloy na pagsubok na kumita sa pamamagitan ng smuggling,” he added.

(This is something we owe to our fellow Filipinos, again, the farmers and fishermen who struggle every day to earn fairly and work honorably, while these smugglers are not ashamed of their continued attempts to profit through smuggling.)
He also warned the public against the danger of consuming smuggled goods.

“Delikado kapag smuggled. Hindi natin alam dahil merong epekto sa kalusugan. Hindi sila kumukuha ng tamang permiso sa Department of Agriculture, in particular halimbawa sa DTI (Department of Trade and Industry)… Delikado,” he said.

(It is dangerous when it is smuggled. We don’t know because it has an effect on health. They do not obtain the proper permits from the Department of Agriculture, particularly, for example, from the DTI… It is dangerous.)
Nepomuceno said that the respondent BOC officials are now under preventive suspension.
Meanwhile, Nepomuceno said that the BOC will also file a complaint for violation of the Anti-Agricultural Sabotage Act of 2024 (AAES).
“Itong P17 million na ito ay lagpas sa threshold na tinatawag ng AAES. Ang threshold po ay P10 milyon. Kaya ito, sasampahan din natin ng violation ng AAES,” he said.
(This P17 million is above the threshold set by the AAES. The threshold is P10 million. So we will also file a [complaint for] violation of the AAES.)
In total, the BOC has conducted 1,882 operations, recovering smuggled goods worth P84 billion, according to the commissioner.
Of the P84 billion, he said that almost P14 billion were due to agricultural smuggling. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: SEC witness: Law does not require firms to declare dividends
articles.summary: The Corporation Code does not require companies to declare dividends it paid to its stockholders, a witness from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said Tuesday.

blocks.text: Published September 22, 2026 11:22am
The Corporation Code does not require companies to declare dividends it paid to its stockholders, a witness from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said Tuesday.
SEC Company Registration and Monitoring Department Director Gerardo del Rosario made the testimony during Day 28 of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial.

Cross-examined by defense lawyer Justin Gular, Del Rosario said Section 42 of the Corporation Code states that “the board of directors of a stock corporation may declare dividends out of the unrestricted retained earnings which shall be payable in cash, property, or in stock to all stockholders on the basis of outstanding stock held by them.”
Asked if the phrase “may declare” means such declaration is not mandatory, Del Rosario said, “Tama po.” (You are correct.)
Del Rosario earlier testified 10 of the 18 firms which the Vice President or her husband Manases Carpio have interest in did not declare dividends in multiple years covering years 2004 to 2025.
He also said that eight of the 18 firms did not submit any annual financial statements, meaning the SEC did not have information to determine if these companies paid dividends.
On Tuesday, Del Rosario testified that Section 42 of the Corporation Code provides certain exemptions in declaring dividends such as:

items: (a) when justified by definite corporate expansion projects or programs approved by the board of directors; or

(b) when the corporation is prohibited under any loan agreement with financial institutions or creditors, whether local or foreign, from declaring dividends without their consent, and such consent has not yet been secured; or
(c) when it can be clearly shown that such retention is necessary under special circumstances obtaining in the corporation, such as when there is need for special reserve for probable contingencies.

blocks.text: Gular then argued that Section 3.i of the Code of Conduct for Public Officials and Employees states that the crime of conflict of interest is only committed when a public official is a substantial shareholder or has substantial interest in the firm.
Asked by Gular if he is in the position to determine whether the Vice President is a substantial shareholder or has substantial interest in the 18 firms discussed, Del Rosario said “No.”

Gular also asked the SEC official if he has access to information on inheritance, sale of properties, appraised value of land, which could account for the assets of the Vice President other than the dividends from the 18 firms, and Del Rosario replied no since these records are outside of the SEC’s mandate. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Tilbury LNG facility in Delta, B.C. gets greenlight for expansion
articles.summary: Approval came immediately after the provincial government issued an environmental assessment certificate to FortisBC. The project involves adding a new storage tank and equipment to produce 7,700…

image.caption: The FortisBC Tilbury LNG project in Delta, B.C., is pictured in November 2015. An expansion proposal for the project has been approved by both the provincial and federal governments. (Jonathan Hayward/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: British Columbia·New

Approval came immediately after the provincial government issued an environmental assessment certificate to FortisBC. The project involves adding a new storage tank and equipment to produce 7,700 tonnes of liquefied natural gas per day.
The province says the project could generate 100 permanent jobs
The federal government has approved expansion of the Tilbury LNG facility in Delta, B.C., saying potential adverse effects are justified by the project's benefits.

Monday's approval under the "one project, one review" principle came immediately after the B.C. government issued an environmental assessment certificate to FortisBC for the project on Tilbury Island in the Fraser River.

The province says the project could generate 6,200 full-time-equivalent years of employment during construction and 100 permanent jobs, and contribute up to $1.7 billion to provincial GDP during construction.
Federal Environment Minister Julie Dabrusin says in a statement the project shows how to "create jobs and grow the economy while protecting the environment and advancing reconciliation."
The project involves adding a large new storage tank and equipment to produce up to 7,700 tonnes of liquefied natural gas per day.

But it has faced opposition from within the B.C. government, with Kelly Greene, minister of emergency management and climate readiness, saying in July she was "disappointed" by FortisBC's decision to move forward with the project, citing safety concerns.

"For months, I have listened to safety concerns from people in my community. I raised those issues with government at every opportunity. I am disappointed with FortisBC's decision, as I know many of those I represent will be," she said at the time.

Greene said her opposition had remained unchanged since before she was elected to the legislature, while B.C. NDP Premier David Eby said his government has a "big tent," which allowed Greene to criticize the plan.
Federal Energy Minister Tim Hodgson called the approval "a step forward in our mission to get major nation-building projects built faster."

"Today's approval of the Tilbury Phase 2 LNG expansion project will power [B.C.] Ferries with cleaner fuel, strengthen Canada's energy security and create economic opportunities for British Columbians," he said on social media on Monday.
The B.C. government had touted the expansion as helping meet rising demand for LNG at the Port of Vancouver and improving access to fuel for vessels that travel the coast and across the Pacific.

items: B.C. government clears regulatory path for Delta's LNG pipeline expansion

blocks.text: The province said in a statement on Monday that the environmental assessment certificate included "18 legally binding conditions related to air quality, wildlife protection, greenhouse-gas reduction, health and emergency planning, and ongoing monitoring of impacts to First Nations."
It said the Environmental Assessment Office sought consensus with 12 Indigenous nations, while 13 other Indigenous groups were informed of key milestones.
The assessment process was initiated in February 2020, but the province said it was delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, and FortisBC submitted a revised application in February 2026.

The STAR / Michael Varcas
MANILA, Philippines — A major transport group is set to hold a two-day nationwide transport strike on September 29 and 30 as rising fuel prices continue to squeeze drivers' earnings.

Pagkakaisa ng mga Samahan ng Tsuper at Operator Nationwide (PISTON) announced on Tuesday, September 22, that at least 70,000 jeepney drivers and operators are expected to join the strike, along with groups representing workers, the urban poor and commuters.
PISTON National President Mody Floranda said affected routes and areas in Metro Manila include:

blocks.text: Floranda appealed for understanding from commuters who may be affected by the strike, stressing that rising fuel prices also drive up the cost of basic goods and services.

"Tayo ay nananawagan sa ating mga commuters, sapagkat sa bawat pagtataas ng presyo ng petrolyo, ang kaakibat niyan ay pagtaas ng mga bilihin at halos hindi na makasabay ang maliliit na sahod at kita ng ating mamamayan," Floranda said in an interview with dzMM.
("We are appealing to our commuters because every increase in fuel prices comes with higher prices of goods, while our people's low wages and incomes can barely keep up.")
Among the groups' demands are the immediate suspension of value-added and excise taxes on fuel products, the scrapping of the Oil Deregulation Law, higher wages for workers and a fare increase.
Floranda said other transport groups are welcome to join the strike at the end of the month.
Three major fuel price hikes this September have driven up diesel prices by a total of P18.31 per liter, kerosene by P16.67 and gasoline by P15.25.
The latest round of increases took effect Tuesday, with diesel rising by P8.82 per liter, kerosene by P6.47 and gasoline by P4.88.
The Department of Energy has said upward pressure on fuel prices could persist until the end of the year as tensions in the Middle East continue to affect global oil supply.

articles.title: Baste Duterte: Davao City unaware of VP Sara's GenCorp interests
articles.summary: VP Sara declared GenCorp in her SALN. Her brother says Davao City never knew.

blocks.text: September 22, 2026 | 10:01am

MANILA, Philippines — Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte said city officials were unaware that Vice President Sara Duterte had declared an interest in GenCorp Industries Inc., which had secured 19 contracts with the local government worth more than P33.2 million.
Baste made the statement in a post on his Facebook account late Monday, September 21, a day before he is scheduled to appear as a witness in his sister’s impeachment trial.
“I, and all other officials and employees of the City Government of Davao, never had any knowledge of Vice President Sara Z. Duterte holding an interest in GENCORP INDUSTRIES INC.,” he said.
Baste also said the vice president’s name or the surname “Duterte” did not appear in GenCorp’s official documents submitted for the transactions with the city.
“Neither the name Sara Zimmerman Duterte nor the surname ‘Duterte’ appears in any of the official documents, such as, among others, the Articles of Incorporation,” he said.
The mayor said GenCorp underwent evaluation for each transaction and was found to have submitted the lowest calculated responsive bid or offer.
He added that all 19 transactions were processed, reported and published through the Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System.
Of the 19 contracts, 13 had been completed while six were still ongoing, Baste said.
Four of the contracts were secured through competitive public bidding, while 15 were undertaken through small-value procurement.
The mayor said the transactions were above board. He also challenged anyone making allegations against the city government’s dealings with GenCorp to present verified and reliable evidence.
“I remain steadfast in my commitment to transparency, fairness and the absolute truth,” Baste said.
“This statement is issued ahead of any so-called lawful proceedings as I believe that the people, especially the people of the City of Davao, have the right to know,” he added.
SEC testimony
Baste’s statement came after the issue of Duterte’s business interests was raised during the 27th day of her impeachment trial on Monday.

Securities and Exchange Commission Company Registration and Monitoring Department Director Gerardo Fernando del Rosario testified that Duterte remained a shareholder and member of the board of directors of Metro City Chow Foods Corporation after she assumed office as vice president in 2022.
SEC records presented during the proceedings showed Duterte remained on the company’s board from 2022 to 2025. She was also listed as a 20% shareholder.

The prosecution cited Article VII, Section 13 of the 1987 Constitution, which prohibits the president, vice president, Cabinet members and their deputies or assistants from holding another office or employment during their tenure. The provision also bars them from directly or indirectly practicing another profession or participating in any business during their term.

Del Rosario, however, said it would be up to the Senate to determine whether Duterte’s continued role in the company constituted a violation of the Constitution. The SEC itself had not made such a determination.
The Metro City Chow Foods testimony is separate from GenCorp.
Duterte declared GenCorp as one of her business interests in her 2024 and 2025 Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth.

During Monday’s hearing, however, Del Rosario said Duterte’s name did not appear as an incorporator, director or stockholder in GenCorp’s corporate records. The company’s records instead identified JTC Group of Companies Philippines Inc. as its largest subscriber.

Del Rosario said a person could potentially have an indirect interest in GenCorp through JTC if that person controlled the latter company, but the corporate records presented to the impeachment court did not list Duterte directly in GenCorp.
Davao transactions
The prosecution is expected to examine the Davao City government’s transactions with GenCorp when Baste takes the witness stand.

Prosecution counsel Benjamin Tolosa Jr. earlier said Baste’s testimony would focus on whether GenCorp, which Duterte identified in her SALN as a business interest, had dealings with the Davao City government. The testimony is also expected to touch on allegations that Duterte failed to divest from business interests while serving as vice president.
Baste is scheduled to testify from September 28 to 30.

The impeachment trial will continue to discuss Article II of the Articles of Impeachment, which includes allegations involving Duterte’s wealth, SALN disclosures and alleged continued business interests while in office. — with a report from Ian Laqui

articles.title: Canadian province sues OpenAI over Tumbler Ridge school shooting
articles.summary: British Columbia has accused the company of failing to report the shooter's troubling interactions with ChatGPT to law enforcement.

blocks.text: A Canadian province is suing OpenAI over its alleged failure to notify authorities about concerning user interactions on ChatGPT prior to the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting.
The company has previously apologised for not flagging Jessie Van Rootselaar's account to law enforcement before the 18-year-old killed eight people, including six children, in February.

British Columbia attorney general Niki Sharma said the lawsuit, filed to a US federal court on Monday, raised questions about "the responsibilities of technology companies when they become aware of credible threats of serious violence".
Families of those killed or injured in the shooting have filed separate lawsuits against OpenAI.

Media reports revealed that Van Rootselaar's ChatGPT activity was flagged by OpenAI's safety team for references to gun violence months before the attack, but the company did not alert local authorities.
In April, OpenAI's chief executive Sam Altman apologised to the families of the victims.
"I am deeply sorry that we did not alert law enforcement," Altman wrote in an open letter.
The BBC has requested comment from OpenAI regarding the latest lawsuit.
"To date, OpenAI has not taken meaningful steps to address the concerns raised by survivors, families and the Tumbler Ridge community," Sharma said in a statement.
"The company still has an opportunity to demonstrate accountability by strengthening safeguards, improving transparency and taking concrete action to help prevent similar tragedies in the future."
Speaking to reporters on Monday, Sharma said she had not read the contents of the OpenAI chats.
"We have asked OpenAI to disclose these chats. They have refused. We should all be asking them: Why?" she said, according to CBC, external.
Sharma said the lawsuit was filed in California, as the alleged decision not to report the shooter's ChatGPT account occurred in that US state, according to AFP.
Sharma told reporters that any financial damages won by the province would go towards rebuilding the secondary school.

articles.title: Lithuania ready to 'fight back' but has evacuation plans in face of Russia threats, PM tells BBC
articles.summary: Sinkevičius told BBC Newsnight Lithuanians feel "constantly threatened" by Moscow, but the nation was prepared to "fight back" if attacked.

blocks.text: Lithuania's prime minister has told the BBC his country has made evacuation plans in the face of threats from Russia, but added they "will not surrender" if attacked.
Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius told Newsnight that Lithuanians feel "constantly threatened" by Russia, in part because of drones entering the nation's airspace.

He told Newsnight if his country was attacked, "we will fight back... we will engage". But he said there were plans for a "variety of scenarios" and used an example of getting elderly citizens out of cities "smoothly" and avoiding traffic jams.
Lithuania, a Nato member, shares a land border with the Russian enclave of Kaliningrad.
"We're thinking about a variety of scenarios, not all of them are being discussed very much publicly," Sinkevičius told the BBC.
"We face concrete threats, not on a daily basis, but we're experiencing them and it's a true reality for us."
Sinkevičius also said the UK needed a "shift in the mindset" in terms of its approach to defence, but noted that Lithuania was "closer to the border and closer to [the] threat".
It comes just a week after Nato fighter pilots shot down a drone that entered Lithuania's airspace.

Though the origins of the drone have not been confirmed, Lithuanian Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas told Newshour that it came from the direction of Belarus, Lithuania's neighbour and a key Russian ally.
The UK's Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said: "Thanks to the swift and professional actions of Lithuanian and Italian forces, Nato once again demonstrated our readiness to protect our airspace.
"We stand united, around the clock, in defence of every inch of Nato territory."
Moscow did not comment on the incident.

blocks.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

There are four articles of impeachment against Duterte involving alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Only 21 out of 24 senator-judges are physically present. Senator Bato dela Rosa remains in hiding as he faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Senator Jinggoy Estrada has been detained and suspended in connection with a plunder case, and Senator Rodante Marcoleta surrendered to authorities as he also faces a plunder case.
